doc: VALUE-BINDING radar for the session TOP-UP verifiers. These cases exist
because every SDK's top-up verifier only asks the RPC 'did this signature
confirm?' and never asks 'does the confirmed transaction actually raise
THIS channel's deposit by newDeposit-oldDeposit?'. The Go verifier comment
says it outright: 'the new deposit is trusted as provided'. So a confirmed
but UNRELATED signature (a real transaction that landed on-chain but is not
a top-up of this channel for this delta) is accepted, and the merchant
raises the deposit / credit line on no on-chain proof at all. This is the
The mock RPC in the executable driver models 'confirmed but unrelated': it
reports a fixed set of real landed signatures as confirmed and everything
else as not-found. It has NO notion of channel/delta binding — exactly the
shape a production RPC's getSignatureStatuses has. A verifier that passes
these cases is conflating 'signature confirmed' with 'signature proves this
deposit', which is the whole hole.

cases.description: A confirmed but UNRELATED signature (a real landed transaction that is not a top-up of this channel) is paired with an inflated newDeposit that is still <= cap. The signature confirms on-chain, so a confirmation-only verifier accepts and raises the deposit with zero proof the funds landed.
cases.pendingFix: top-up verifier must fetch the confirmed transaction and assert its channel top_up instruction raises THIS channel's deposit to newDeposit (delta binding), not merely that the signature confirmed.

cases.description: The signature belongs to a REAL, confirmed top-up transaction, but its on-chain deposit delta is small (e.g. +1) while the payload claims a large newDeposit (delta +3999999). A verifier that only confirms the signature cannot see the mismatch and accepts the inflated deposit.
cases.pendingFix: top-up verifier must compare the confirmed transaction's on-chain deposit delta against newDeposit-oldDeposit and reject on mismatch.

cases.description: The C1 shape applied to top-up: a placeholder/empty signature submitted while an RPC IS configured. With an RPC present the verifier is asserting it can prove the top-up on-chain, so a signature that carries no such proof must be rejected fleet-wide — the same way verifyOpenTx rejects the placeholder open under the C1 guard.
cases.note: VERIFIED GREEN on TS src: the empty signature is fed to getSignatureStatuses, which returns no status, so handleTopUp rejects with 'not found'. The rejection is incidental (not-found), not an explicit placeholder guard — kept as a regression guard so a future change that short-circuits the RPC on a placeholder does not silently accept.
cases.pendingFix: none for TS; a dedicated placeholder guard mirroring the verifyOpenTx C1 guard would make the intent explicit. Confirm Go/Python behave the same in-runner.
